title: Write a README for a CLI tool
persona: Pooja, B.Tech 3rd year, first open-source contribution
scenario: You built a CLI tool that bulk-renames files based on EXIF dates from photos (handy for trip photos). It works on macOS and Linux, not Windows. You want a README that gets a stranger from ‘what is this’ to ‘installed and used it’ in under 90 seconds. You hate READMEs that bury the install command under a paragraph about why the author built it.
badPrompt: write a README for my CLI tool that renames files using EXIF dates
badOutput:
# My CLI Tool

A command-line tool to rename files based on EXIF dates.

## Features
- Renames files
- Uses EXIF data
- Easy to use

## Installation
Clone the repo and run setup.

## Usage
Run the command with your files.

## License
MIT.

hints.title: Force the 90-second test
hints.body: ‘Stranger lands → installed and used in under 90 seconds.’ This dictates structure, install command first, story later.

hints.title: Lead with one usage example
hints.body: ‘First non-title content: one copy-paste-able command and what it does.’ Beats every ‘Features’ section.

checks.tip: Anchor the function, EXIF-based file renaming for photos.
Surface platform support, macOS/Linux only, not Windows.
Lock the constraint, stranger to ‘installed and used’ in 90 seconds.
Force a no-‘why I built this’ paragraph at the top.
Anchor the audience, a stranger landing cold.
Lead with install + usage. The action, not the story.
Specify the section order, install → usage example → flags → caveats.
Demand copy-paste-able command blocks, not prose.

tipIfLow: READMEs fail when they lead with the author's story. The unlock is the 90-second test, locking the section order (install → example → flags → caveats), and surfacing the platform constraint (macOS/Linux, not Windows) up top. Strangers won't read past line 5.
goldPrompt: Act as a docs writer. I'm Pooja, 3rd-year B.Tech, this is my first open-source contribution. The CLI bulk-renames files based on EXIF dates. Works on macOS + Linux, NOT Windows. Goal: a stranger lands → installs → uses it in under 90 seconds. Output the README in this exact order: (1) 1-line description, (2) ONE copy-paste install command, (3) ONE usage example with the actual output, (4) flags table, (5) caveats including the Windows non-support, (6) license. Refuse to lead with 'why I built this' or 'features' bullets. Cap at 200 lines.
